items.title: Been thinking about why AI diffusion has been slow
items.text: Been thinking about why AI diffusion has been slow. It’s because we are asking users to understand our nerdy lab speak. We greet them with a blank window and ask them to write a prompt. Then they have to pick a model, decide whether they need an agent, and somehow know what context windows, reasoning, MCP, memory, and skills are. Most people don’t care. They need a thing done. If you can give them something that does that, they’re happy. I think we will see that breakthrough product in the next 12 months.

items.title: Correct take
items.text: Correct take. 99% of tokens in the world will get consumed in an enterprise context. They will be for writing code, combing through insane amounts of life sciences research, automating manufacturing, securing enterprises, detecting fraud, and thousands of other tasks like this that have significant economic value. This is both where the cost of AI can be most justified but also where the impact of parallel workers doing tasks on your behalf is most useful. Even the agents that most impact consumers will often be wrapped up as just end to end services where the consumer doesn’t think about there being an AI system on the other end, like faster insurance or onboarding to a bank.
